transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (CISO, Alpine Med), Tom Alvarez (Head of IT), Meera Patel (Compliance Manager)

Summary:
Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 / ISO 27001 coverage, trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO integration, audit logs and encryption/KMS. Customer is evaluating Redwood for both hosted API and a Private (VPC) deployment for PHI workloads; main asks are evidence (reports), control mappings, and architecture details for key management and network isolation.

Topics:
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001 certificate availability
- Trust center and documentation access (read-only)
- Controls mapping from Redwood product controls to SOC 2 and ISO clauses
- RBAC, SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning
- Audit logging granularity and retention options
- Encryption at-rest and in-transit, KMS/HSM integrations
- Data residency and private deployment architecture (VPC, on-prem options)

Action items (captured in metadata): Sofia to share reports and trust center, Ethan to send controls mapping, customer to confirm residency and stakeholders.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: All right, thanks everyone for joining, um, appreciate you carving out time. This is Sofia from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Ethan, our solutions engineer. Today we wanted to walk through SOC 2 and ISO posture and answer any specific questions you have.
[00:12] Rachel: Thanks Sofia. I'm Rachel, CISO at Alpine Med. Quick context, we have internal auditors asking for a controls matrix showing gaps and how Redwood maps to our SOC 2 baseline. We also need to understand SSO, RBAC, and where audit logs live.
[00:25] Ethan: Great, thanks Rachel. I can start with the evidence side, we publish a SOC 2 Type II report annually and we have an ISO 27001 certificate as well, both available in the trust center. I will send the temporary read-only access link after the call.
[00:37] Tom: Quick clarification, are those reports redacted or full reports? Our procurement team needs the full attestations if possible.
[00:43] Sofia: So usually we share the full SOC 2 Type II attestation under an NDA, and the ISO cert is public. For more detailed control narratives we provide a controls mapping spreadsheet that correlates Redwood controls to SOC 2 and ISO clauses.
[00:55] Rachel: Ok that's, that's helpful. Also on the KMS piece, we need to know whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys for the private deployment and if HSM is an option.
[01:05] Ethan: Yes, for Redwood Private we support BYOK via customer KMS. We have integrations with AWS KMS (and you can bring your own CMK), and for on-prem/HSM there are partner integrations. There was a note in the docs that HSM-backed key wraps are supported via our key management plugin, but I will include the exact doc link.
[01:22] Meera: For audit logs, what's the retention and do logs include user-level actions, like token creation, model deployment, configuration changes?
[01:29] Ethan: We capture admin actions, API keys operations, model rollouts, route changes, and per-request telemetry. Retention defaults are 90 days in hosted but can be extended for Dedicated/Private and exported to your SIEM via syslog or S3 sink. I'll include sample log entries in the controls mapping.
[01:44] Rachel: And are logs tamper-evident or do you provide integrity proofs?
[01:49] Ethan: We don't currently provide blockchain-style attestations, however audit trails are append-only in our system and we maintain checksums and access logs; for higher assurance in Private deployments you can ship logs to your own immutable storage.
[02:05] Tom: On SSO, we use Okta. How does Redwood handle provisioning, SCIM, and role mapping?
[02:11] Sofia: We support SAML and OIDC for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Role mapping supports Role Based Access Control with customizable roles; out of the box we have Admin, Dev, ReadOnly and you can add finer grained permissions in Private.
[02:24] Ethan: Small note, sometimes the product naming in the docs is a little off - you might see Redwood Console or Redwood Dedicated in the trust center - but the underlying RBAC model is consistent across products.
[02:35] Rachel: Our auditors will want to see specific control mappings to CC6, CC7 and to ISO controls A.9 and A.10. Can you map those?
[02:43] Ethan: Yep - we'll map Redwood controls to SOC 2 Common Criteria such as logical access, change management, encryption, and to ISO Annex A controls. We'll put that in the spreadsheet and call out any shared responsibilities - for example network segmentation in a Private deployment vs hosted where we provide managed networking.
[02:58] Meera: Data residency - we host some PHI in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, do you offer region pinning and are there transfer logs?
[03:06] Sofia: For hosted customers we can pin region for data residency on paid tiers; for Dedicated and Private you always control region and network. Transfer logs can be provided via our audit exports and we can add metadata to requests indicating region and customer tenancy.
[03:20] Tom: Is there any customer data stored in logs that could be a compliance problem? For example are prompts or embeddings retained?
[03:28] Ethan: By default we retain request metadata and model outputs per retention policy; for enterprise contracts we can configure no retention or encryption-only retention. We also support differential privacy options at the model layer, but that typically requires model-level config. I'll surface the exact policy excerpts.
[03:44] Rachel: Ok, one more from procurement - encryption in transit, TLS versions supported, and cipher suites.
[03:50] Ethan: We enforce TLS 1.2+ by default, we prefer TLS 1.3 where supported, and we use modern cipher suites. For FIPS or specific cipher requirements on Private deployments, we can enable FIPS-approved modules and HSM-backed TLS if needed.
[04:03] Meera: On the controls mapping, can you also indicate which controls are 'Redwood responsibility' vs 'Customer responsibility' - we need that for our gap analysis.
[04:11] Sofia: Absolutely, the mapping spreadsheet will have a column for Responsibility (R/C) and notes for implementation detail.
[04:17] Tom: Any third-party subprocessors of note? We need the vendor list for our vendor risk team.
[04:22] Ethan: Yes, list includes cloud providers like AWS/GCP, monitoring vendors, and security tooling partners; the trust center has the current list and we'll share the vendor/subprocessor CSV.
[04:32] Rachel: If we go Private, what's the onboarding timeline and what evidence will you produce for our auditors after deployment?
[04:39] Sofia: Private onboarding typically 6-8 weeks depending on network setup and KMS/HSM integration. For auditors we provide architecture diagrams, configuration baselines, hardening docs, and environment-specific logs and attestations as part of the enterprise package.
[04:54] Meera: A small note - sometimes the terms in the SOC report use Redwood product names that our audit team doesn't recognize, is there a crosswalk?
[04:59] Ethan: Yes we include a crosswalk table in the trust center that maps product names and components to the control descriptions, we'll make sure it's included in the packet.
[05:08] Rachel: Sounds good. On legal, is there a standard DPA and can we get redlines?
[05:13] Sofia: We have a standard DPA and security addendum; we can provide a copy, and legal is open to redlines for enterprise contracts but that will go through our Legal ops.
[05:22] Tom: For the KMS, if we bring our own key in AWS KMS, does Redwood ever have access to unencrypted plaintext keys?
[05:29] Ethan: No, with BYOK we use envelope encryption; Redwood services never have access to your raw key material. The CMK in your account performs decryption and we receive encrypted wrapped keys. I'll include the crypto flow diagram.
[05:41] Meera: Regarding audit log retention - is there an option for immutability or WORM storage for logs?
[05:47] Ethan: For Private we can configure log sinks to S3 with Object Lock or send to your SIEM for immutability. For hosted we can provide exports and also integrate with third-party immutability offerings on request.
[06:00] Rachel: Ok I think we have what we need for now. Can you please send the SOC 2 report and the controls mapping by next week?
[06:06] Sofia: Yes, I'll get those out. Ethan will follow up with the spreadsheet and architecture docs.
[06:11] Tom: Thanks, any caveats about shared responsibility on backups or de-duplication?
[06:16] Ethan: Backups are part of the managed service for hosted, in Dedicated/Private you can choose if we manage backups or you do; responsibilities will be spelled out in the controls mapping.
[06:26] Rachel: Great. One minor note - sometimes transcript shows product names a bit off, so if our audit team has questions about terminology, can we set up a short walkthrough of the trust center?
[06:35] Sofia: Definitely, we can schedule a 30-min trust center walkthrough with our docs owner.
[06:40] Meera: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[06:43] Sofia: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the architecture deep dive.
[06:48] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: Speaker overlaps and occasional mis-hear of product names (Redwood Console vs Redwood Control Plane) present; we kept the verbatim speech style and filler words where present.
